content.title: About
content.content: Clams are marine bivalve mollusks that are often prepared by baking or broiling. They have a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a tender yet firm texture. Clams are eaten fresh, as well as canned or incorporated into prepared dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Clams filter water, helping to clean their environment.
In the wild, clams can live for more than 20 years.
They are an important source of protein in many coastal communities worldwide.
Clams feature in diverse cuisines, from French "clams in white wine" to Asian dishes with soy sauce.
There are over 1,000 clam species, but only a few commercial varieties dominate the market.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Clams provide about 10–12 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good source of high‑quality protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: They contain very little saturated fat and have lower calories than most meat products.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for blood formation and nervous system health; clams are one of the best natural sources.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support immune function and various metabolic processes.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Clams provide modest amounts of EPA and DHA, beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to clams, ranging from mild symptoms to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Clams can accumulate toxins and heavy metals from polluted waters; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: Elevated purines may exacerbate gout symptoms in susceptible people.

items.title: Need for proper cooking
items.content: Raw clams may harbor pathogenic bacteria; they should be cooked until shells fully open.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Clams can be baked in the oven with herbs, garlic, and lemon or quickly broiled on a grill pan with butter. They are commonly served in sauces, soups, pastas, and salads. Before cooking, rinse thoroughly and remove the “beard” – the fibrous thread that protrudes from the shell.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh clams should be kept in the refrigerator in a tightly sealed container covered with a damp cloth, and used within 1–2 days. Frozen clams store best at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Discard any clams with open or cracked shells before cooking.
